report:
Fresh followup review of meta.reviews.summary_format. Preserved the prior input/output, started a fresh review and read the complete claim, sole implementation association and both associated tests. Recaptured all prior additional dependencies: review fixture helpers lines 1–118, fragment_freshness claim, invalid_reports_and_stale_inputs_never_complete_an_active_review, lib.rs and check.rs. Compared all fragments by path/selector and implementation/test metadata. The only differences are a placeholder_status comment association in review.rs and a validation_layout attribute on unsupported_versions_and_mismatched_identity_cannot_pass. No behavior, test assertions, claim, metadata for this anchor or helper changed; no captures were removed. I evaluated that delta against the complete prior assessment and current source rather than blindly refreshing it.

The ordinary Summary association in review.rs accounts for all five fields: anchor is the complete dotted identity; started_at_unix_seconds is u64 seconds from SystemTime duration_since UNIX_EPOCH; recorded_at_unix_seconds is Option<u64> serialized as null initially, then populated during record after output writing; schema_version and policy_version use separate current constants. start validates the anchor against inventory and creates these fields. record loads/validates the summary, preserves the start time and updates recording time; read_summary rejects mismatched identity and unsupported format/policy versions. These paths all lie in the captured associated file. Timestamps serve as metadata, not freshness evidence: input_errors compares current initial fragments and associations and reselects appended fragments for exact source equality. record rejects stale inputs, while shared check orchestration loads and validates saved records and computes acceptance through the same freshness mechanism. The captured fragment_freshness claim provides the referenced detailed rules.

Both ordinary tests have direct substantive assertions. start_invalidates_previous_success_and_record_is_required reads summary JSON and checks demo.rule, positive start time, initially null recording time, both version constants, and no legacy input_sha256. It restarts a successful review, verifies output removal and unfinished loading, appends a dependency read, then records and verifies unchanged input bytes, recording time at least start time, restored validity and rejection of another record/read after completion. unsupported_versions_and_mismatched_identity_cannot_pass independently corrupts each version and the anchor, asserting failure with matching reason, anchor identity and review guidance. The captured supporting stale-input test changes implementation source, requires record failure, verifies captured input bytes stay unchanged and shared validation remains failing; requested edits also remain failing. Thus freshness is checked against source rather than summary time/digest. Detailed selector behavior remains under the explicitly referenced freshness claim.

No TODO/N/A evidence exists for this anchor. All summary requirements and both tests remain accounted for after the two annotation-only changes. No source edits, tests, formatting or workspace build were performed in this followup; executed review start/read, capture comparison and record only. Prior/central execution was not represented as new execution. No requested edits.
